comparison: Perfect agreement on growth defect claims (C7, C53, C66, C67, C73, C109). Both evaluations find the evidence from growth curves and complementation experiments fully supported. Reviewers explicitly affirmed the findings as 'very carefully performed with appropriate controls.'

Perfect agreement on cell separation and morphology claims (C8, C9, C59-C65, C69, C70, C110). Both evaluations accept the microscopy data showing clustering and separation defects. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'very carefully performed' with no concerns about the morphological findings.

Perfect agreement on ultrastructural claims (C78-C88). Both evaluations accept the cryo-ET data showing unchanged wall thickness but altered septum angles. Peer reviewers note the study 'utilizes compelling methods' and accept these structural findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on genomic characterization claims (C55-C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to potential confounding from the L200F mutation in EFWG_00994, while peer reviewers accept the authors' assessment that most mutations are unlikely to contribute, implicitly accepting the characterization through noting 'appropriate controls and experimental checks.'

Perfect agreement on background claims (C51, C52) establishing that sagA was previously thought essential. Both evaluations accept these claims as properly supported by prior literature, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming the novelty of demonstrating sagA is non-essential.

Strong agreement on antibiotic sensitivity claims (C10, C74-C77, C117). Both evaluations find the MIC data supported. OpenEval explicitly notes the specificity of β-lactam effects and complementation restoration. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of comprehensive characterization without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on in vivo immunotherapy claims (C13, C98-C107, C125). Both evaluations fully accept the tumor growth data, immune profiling, and conclusions about SagA's requirement for ICI activity. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'proof-of-concept for identifying bacterial effectors of immunotherapy response.'

Strong agreement on muropeptide composition claims (C11, C89-C92). Both evaluations accept the LC-MS data showing altered peptidoglycan processing. OpenEval includes additional claims (C15) about complementation. Peer reviewers note the study examined 'impacts on peptidoglycan cleavage' as part of careful work.

Strong agreement on NOD2 activation claims (C12, C93-C95, C123-C124). Both evaluations accept the NOD2 activation assay data. OpenEval emphasizes convergence with muropeptide data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm sagA is 'necessary for the immunogenic and anti-tumor effects' through NOD2 activation.

Agreement on essentiality claims (C18, C108) but with nuance. OpenEval notes potential contradiction between C18 ('essential for growth') and C108 (distinguishing viability from proper growth). Peer reviewers accept the distinction implicitly by characterizing sagA as 'non-essential' while causing 'marked growth defect.'

Partial overlap on complementation claims. OpenEval R10 focuses on catalytic mutant (C71, C72, C17) showing activity requirement. Peer R3 covers broader complementation experiments (C14-C17, C66-C72) and accepts all as 'appropriate controls' without distinguishing the catalytic mutant findings.

Partial overlap on NOD2 requirement in vivo. OpenEval R7 focuses specifically on genetic requirement using Nod2+/- vs Nod2-/- mice (C96, C97, C50, C107). Peer R8 covers broader immunotherapy findings (C13, C96-C107, C125) and accepts all data supporting sagA's necessity for anti-tumor effects.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R19 addresses inference claims (C20, C95) about SagA being essential for immune activation based on convergent evidence. Peer R9 addresses essentiality for growth/viability (C18, C19, C20, C108). Only C20 overlaps, both evaluations support it.

OpenEval evaluates comparative claims (C111-C114) contextualizing SagA with peptidoglycan hydrolases in other species. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess these comparative/contextual claims.

OpenEval rates speculative/future work claims (C115, C116, C119) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are hypotheses rather than demonstrated results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately critique these forward-looking statements.

OpenEval evaluates claims (C32-C50) summarizing prior work from authors' laboratory, finding all properly attributed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess these background claims from previous publications.

OpenEval evaluates taxonomic/conservation claims (C120-C122) about SagA function across Enterococcus species. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess these phylogenetic context claims.

OpenEval evaluates sedimentation phenotype claims (C54, C68) as supported secondary observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess this minor phenotypic detail.
